paper_metadata.title: Grain size dependent tensile behavior of Mg–3%Al alloy at elevated temperatures

evidence.quote: In this study, we experimentally investigate the effect of grain size on the tensile properties of Mg–3%Al alloys at elevated temperatures.
Grain size dependent tensile behavior of Mg–3%Al alloy at elevated temperatures
Commercial elemental powders of Mg and Al with purity of 99.5% were mixed at the weight ratio of 97:3 Mg to Al.

Bulk nanostructured Mg–3%Al alloys were prepared by mechanical alloying followed by conventional sintering and extrusion.

Microcrystalline rods were obtained from processing unmilled powders whereas two different nanocrystalline (NC 20 and NC30) rods were obtained from processing the powders milled to 20 and 30 h respectively.

The rapid decrease in strength with the increase in temperature is caused by the activation of grain boundary sliding.

Since the NC samples have higher grain boundary area per unit volume relative to the microcrystalline samples, at low temperatures the grain boundaries act as obstacles to the migration of dislocations and twinning, if any. At higher temperatures, the grain boundaries are thermally activated and lead to thermally assisted sliding.
The loss of strain hardening is due to the decreased pile-up of dislocations at higher temperature.
the rapid lowering of strain hardening with temperature for the finer grain specimens promotes necking at lower temperatures.
